name: Starter: Romanian
about: Romanian in real, everyday sentences, with each one's words in Romanian order.

words.să: subjunctive marker, often translated as 'to' (as in 'want to drink')
words.chema: to call; cum te cheamă: what's your name
words.vedea: to see; se vedea: to see each other, to meet
words.țară: country; la țară: in the countryside
words.trezi: to wake; se trezi: to wake up
words.culca: to put to bed; se culca: to go to bed
words.plăcea: to please; îmi place: I like
words.ruga: to ask, to beg; vă rog: please
words.rău: bad; îmi pare rău: I'm sorry

imi-pare-bine.about: Literally to-me it-seems good: what you say when you meet someone.

va-rog.about: Literally I ask you (polite); te rog to a friend.

concept.line: The verb's ending changes with who does it: vorbesc (I speak), vorbești (you speak), vorbește (he or she speaks).
Romanian usually leaves out eu, tu and the other subject words, because the verb's ending shows who: Vorbesc (I speak), Plouă (rains).
Nouns are masculine, feminine or neuter, and the words with them match: un băiat înalt (a boy tall), o fată înaltă (a girl tall).

words.means: am = I have; ai = you have

concept.line: My, your and the rest come after the noun, which takes the: fratele meu (brother-the my), sora mea (sister-the my).

words.means: bani = coin; ban (one hundredth of a leu); bani: money
vorbești = you speak; vorbesc = I speak
înțeleg = I understand; înțelegi = you understand
subjunctive marker, often translated as 'to' (as in 'want to drink')

concept.line: A yes-or-no question can keep the order of a statement, with your voice going up, while a question word normally comes first, often with the verb right after it: Unde este gara?

words.means: locuiesc = I live; locuiești = you live; locuiește = lives; locuim = we live
merg = I go; mergi = you go; merge = goes

concept.line: To like something, you say it pleases you: Îmi place cafeaua (to-me pleases coffee-the), so the verb matches the thing you like.
